https://www.theguardian.com/politics/liv.text: Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of UK politics. The mother of PC Andrew Harper said her family are “bitterly disappointed” that her son’s killers remain eligible for early release after the government revised plans to tackle the overcrowding crisis in prisons. Following pressure from victims, MPs and frontline prison officers, rapists, child sexual abusers and groomers will be excluded from the scheme for England and Wales, the government said on Monday. But domestic abusers and killers will still be eligible for early release, including two men jailed for their role in the death of PC Harper, who sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in August 2019. “Quite frankly, we shouldn’t be in this position,” Debbie Adlam, PC Harper’s mother, told BBC Breakfast. She said it was “completely right” that rapists and paedophiles are not going to be released under the government’s latest plans, but added “they shouldn’t have been cons

Photograph: Newscom/Alamy Natalie Harp Trump gave $45,000 to Natalie Harp and other White House aides as holiday gifts The president’s substantial holiday gifts to four White House aides were made public via financial disclosures released by the administration Associated Press Wed 9 Sep 2026 00.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump gave sizable holiday gifts to four White House aides, according to new financial disclosures released by the administration, including $45,000 to executive assistant Natalie Harp. Communications adviser Margo Martin and deputy director of Oval Office operations Chamberlain Harris also received $45,000, while director of Oval Office operations Walt Nauta received a $20,000 gift. The gifts were noted in the staffers’ annual financial disclosure forms that were published by the administration last week. Harp, Martin and Harris make $150,000 annually and Nauta is paid $175,000 a year, according to the White House’s salary disclosure report to Congress. Jon Ossoff went low on Natalie Harp. The plan worked | Moira Donegan Read more A White House official told the Associated Press that Trump “has a longstanding practice of giving Christmas gifts to people in his orbit, including at times employees and aides, both in government and in his time in the private sector.” The official did not say if any other staffers were given similar gifts from the president, but added that the cash gifts were not related to the “individuals’ official government duties, and therefore are entirely permissible under relevant legal and ethical standards.” The disclosures of the gifts were first reported earlier on Tuesday by The Washington Post. Harp is a constant presence by Trump’s side and is known for carrying a portable printer with her so she can print out favourable media coverage and social media posts for the president, who prefers reading important information on paper rather than on a screen. Martin has been working for Trump since his term in the White House. She started as a White House press assistant and followed the president to Palm Beach, Florida, to help run his media operations after he lost the 2020 election to Joe Biden. She returned to the White House with Trump after his 2024 victory. Earlier this year, Trump appointed Harris to serve on the US Commission of Fine Arts, which has oversight over the president’s White House ballroom project. Nauta, who previously served as a valet to Trump, and Mar-a-Lago property manager Carlos De Oliveira were charged in 2023 with conspiring with Trump to obstruct an FBI investigation into classified documents that the Republican took with him when he left the White House after his first term. The charges were dismissed in 2024. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/18/szoc.text: Menü Kereső A Miniszterelnökség előtt tüntettek a szociális ágazat dolgozói, Magyar Péter átvette a követeléseiket Belföld Magyar Péter miniszterelnök a Szociális Ágazatban Dolgozók Szakszervezetének demonstrációján 2026. szeptember 18-án – Fotó: Balogh Zoltán / MTI Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Tüntetést tartottak a szociális ágazatban dolgozók péntek délután az Alkotmány utcában, a Miniszterelnökség épülete előtt. A megmozdulást a Szociális Ágazatban Dolgozók Szakszervezete (SZÁD) szervezte, mert úgy látják, a bérolló szétnyílása ellehetetleníti a szociális ellátórendszerben dolgozók helyzetét. Emiatt azonnali intézkedéseket, legalább 25 százalékos béremelést és jobb munkakörülmények megteremtését várják el a kormánytól. Magyar Péter miniszterelnök kiment a tüntetők közé, és átvette a szociális dolgozók követeléseit a SZÁD elnökétől, Köves Ferenctől. A kormányfő türelmet kért a szociális szektorban dolgozóktól, és azt mondta, jelenleg is dolgoznak a 2027-es költségvetés kialakításán. „A rezsit is egyben fizetjük, a béremelést sem részletekben kérjük!” mottóval meghirdetett demonstrációt azért hívták össze, mert a szektornak korábban ígért, kétlépcsőben megvalósuló 20-25 százalékos béremelés – amely várhatóan figyelembe veszi majd a minimálbér-emelést és az adójóváírást is – elmarad a munkavállalók várakozásától. Az MTI beszámolója szerint a tüntetésen felszólalók a béremelésen kívül jobb munkakörülményeket és az adminisztratív terhek csökkentését is követelték. Problémának nevezték a magas fluktuációt, és azt, hogy a szakmában maradók munkaterhei magasak. A tüntetők szerint a szakma évtizedek óta küzd bérfejlesztésért, de évről évre csak üres ígéreteket és látszatintézkedéseket kaptak. Köves Ferenc, a Szociális Ágazatban Dolgozók Szakszervezetének elnöke azt mondta: tisztában vannak azzal, hogy a Tisza-kormány a szociális szféra helyzetét az előző kormánytól örökölte, de csak a mostani kormány tudja megoldani a helyzetet. „A szociális háló lyukas, egyre lyukasabb, és így egyre többen esnek át rajta” – mondta, hozzátéve: a politikai elit ezt a szakmát mindig elfelejtette. A szakszervezeti vezető utalt Magyar Péter kampányban tett ígéretére, hogy kormányra kerülésükkor azonnali, 25 százalékos béremelést adnak az ágazatnak. „A szeptember az nem azonnali egy kormányalakulást követően” – mondta. Hozzátette: a 25 százalékos azonnali emelés éves szinten 140-150 milliárd forint kiadást jelentene a költségvetésnek, ami a büdzsé 0,3 százaléka. A rendezvényen megjelent Magyar Péter kormányfő és Szabó Imre Szilárd foglalkoztatáspolitikai helyettes államtitkár. Köves Ferenc Magyar Péternek átnyújtotta a szakszervezet bértáblajavaslatát és azon pontok jegyzékét, amelyekről szeretnének tárgyalni a béremelésen kívül. Magyar a Miniszterelnökség épületébe hívta tárgyalni Kövest és a tüntetés többi szervezőjét, de ezt ők most elutasították, de Köves azt mondta, jövő héten szívesen egyeztetnek a kormány tagjaival. A miniszterelnök a tüntetőkhöz szólva azt mondta, a kormány pontosan tisztában van a szociális ágazat helyzetével, pontosan ismeri annak problémáit, és tudja, még egy 25 százalékos béremelés sem jelent érdemi és valós megoldást a szektorban. Magyar szerint a kormány felelőssége sokrétű, egyszerre kell megoldani a szociális, az egészségügyi, a rendvédelmi és az oktatási ágazat bérproblémáit. A miniszterelnök szerint egy totálisan összeomlott és kivéreztetett költségvetést vettek át a Fidesztől, és neki nemcsak a szociális szférában dolgozók, hanem „minden ember szemébe bele kell tudnia nézni”. Magyar azt mondta, a jövő évi költségvetés tárgyalása jelenleg is zajlik, és ennek végét október 15-re ígérte. Magyar szerint dönteni kell arról, hogy idén egyszeri juttatást és jövő évi béremelést, vagy kétlépcsős béremelést kapnak-e az ágazat dolgozói. A miniszterelnök szerint a tüntetők nyitott kapukat döngetnek a követeléseikkel, és „nagyon-nagy tisztelettel” türelmet kért a szociális ágazat munkavállalóitól. Pintér Sándor volt belügyminiszterre utalva megjegyezte, hogy egy „nyugdíjas rendőr” helyett már külön minisztérium és államtitkárok foglalkoznak a szociális és gyermekvédelmi területtel. „Mindenki tudja, hogy az előző kormány hogyan bánt ezzel a szektorral” – mondta, hozzátéve: hálás a szociális ágazatban dolgozók munkájáért, és igyekeznek sok mindent jóvá tenni abból, amit az elmúlt években, évtizedekben a szektor elszenvedett. „Egy hónap alatt, fél év alatt nem lehet minden problémát megoldani” – mondta Magyar, majd megismételte, hogy a 25 százalékos emelés sem jelent bérfelzárkóztatást, de más szakmákra is gondolniuk kell. Newsflash Newsroom , 07.09.2026, 20:00 WAR – US envoy Steve Witkoff, who was sent by Donald Trump to Moscow and Kyiv, spoke on Monday of “substantial progress” during the visit, with a view to resuming negotiations aimed at ending the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, AFP reports. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner presented the parties with a peace proposal from President Donald Trump. Following the US envoys’ visits to Moscow and Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that he was preparing the next stages of the negotiations. After talks in Moscow, President Vladimir Putin reiterated that Ukraine must give up sovereignty over a substantial part of its territory. US mediation efforts since Donald Trump returned to power have led to several rounds of talks between Moscow and Kyiv in 2025, but these failed to produce results, and the process has stalled since the outbreak of the war in the Middle East in February, AFP also reports. WILDFIRE – Around 20 Romanian firefighters are currently assisting Bulgarian authorities in tackling wildfires on Boril Island. According to the General Inspectorate for Emergencies, the team is working to reduce the risk of the fire spreading, protect local communities and limit the impact on affected areas. Meanwhile, on Saturday, the 69 Romanian firefighters who had spent two weeks operating in Serbia returned home after helping their counterparts in the neighboring country battle wildfires which affected large areas and entire communities. A third contingent of 40 Romanian firefighters arrived in Greece last week, replacing teams which had spent two weeks tackling fires in the country. DEFENCE– Romania’s President, Nicuşor Dan, convened on Monday a meeting of the Supreme Council of National Defence. According to the Presidential Administration, the agenda included the ten-year military procurement plan, an analysis document on the implementation of the SAFE programme, approved last month, as well as the strengthening of the US military presence in Romania. Other current national security issues were also discussed, the Presidential Administration said. PM – Romania’s President, Nicuşor Dan, is expected to announce his candidate for prime minister in the coming days. The PNL and USR, both right-wing parties which, together with the UDMR, are currently supporting Romania’s interim government in Bucharest, have categorically refused to join a government alongside the PSD, the left-wing party now in opposition. The PSD says it is ready to build a parliamentary majority to support a single-party government made up of its own ministers, or a broader cabinet formed around the PSD. Meanwhile, the nationalist opposition, represented by AUR, which has been gaining strongly in the opinion polls, is calling for early elections. Romania has not had a stable government since the beginning of May, following the passage in Parliament of a no-confidence motion against the cabinet led by liberal Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, who continues to serve as caretaker prime minister. ECONOMY – Romania’s economy remained unchanged in the second quarter of this year compared with the first quarter, but contracted by 2% compared with the same period last year, according to data published by the National Institute of Statistics (INS). Construction made the largest positive contribution, following a 12.3% increase in activity, while transport, retail and the hospitality sector weighed on the economy. Household consumption fell by 2.5%, while imports grew faster than exports, the INS data also showed. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/21/thre.text: Three South Korean military officers were injured in an explosion during an operation near the heavily mined border with North Korea, Seoul's military said on Monday.The incident occurred south of the Military Demarcation Line inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), one of the world's most heavily fortified and mined frontiers.Two of the injured officers were evacuated by helicopter, while a third was due to be transported by road before being airlifted, the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said.It was not immediately clear whether the explosion was caused by a North Korean mine, a South Korean mine or another explosive device.The three officers "were injured by an explosion of unknown cause while conducting an operation at a location south of the MDL," the JCS said in a statement.The military did not immediately provide details on the severity of their injuries.The DMZ is a 248-kilometre (154-mile) long and roughly four-kilometre (2.5-mile) wide buffer zone that has divided the Korean Peninsula since the 1953 armistice that halted the Korean War.While the zone itself is officially demilitarised, its northern and southern boundaries are among the world's most heavily fortified frontiers and remain littered with landmines.Around 800,000 mines are estimated to be buried around the area, according to military data cited by Yonhap news agency, many dating to the Korean War although mine-laying has continued in recent years.Since 2024, after North Korean leader Kim Jong-un designated South Korea as his country's "principal enemy," Pyongyang's military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the border as part of efforts to permanently seal off the frontier.South Korea's military has previously said several North Korean soldiers were killed or wounded in accidental mine explosions during those works.Landmine incidents have previously heightened tensions between the two Koreas.In 2015, two South Korean soldiers were seriously wounded when a landmine exploded on the southern side of the DMZ, with one losing both legs.Seoul concluded that North Korean troops had crossed the MDL to plant the mines, an accusation Pyongyang denied.The incident prompted South Korea to resume anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts along the border.The latest incident comes as South Korean President Lee Jae-myung has repeatedly called for unconditional dialogue with the North, overtures that have so far gone unanswered by Pyongyang.

https://www.politico.eu/article/von-der-.text: BRUSSELS — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wants EU leaders to look into the idea of developing bloc-wide strategic gas reserves amid concerns the continent faces a winter shortage, three diplomats and two EU officials told POLITICO. Europe’s existing gas storage caverns — which are typically refilled over the course of the year by commercial actors — are running at record lows this year after high summer prices linked to the war in Iran undercut market incentives to restock, leaving the bloc underprepared for winter. While it wasn't immediately clear to diplomatic officials what form the reserve idea would take, one senior EU official described it as a long-term measure to cushion the bloc against future supply risks, as countries already do with oil and refined products. The Commission president's comments came at a major summit of European leaders in Brussels on Thursday. Advertisement Advertisement Documents detailing November plans to revamp the bloc’s gas security architecture, seen earlier this year by POLITICO, include plans to encourage better crisis management by companies. However, they stop short of explicitly endorsing strategic reserves that governments would have to fill to a set level to offset supply shortages, regardless of market conditions. Countries that typically rely on commercial refilling have already been forced to change tack this year as the limits of the existing model became clear. The Netherlands has moved to subsidize energy purchases , costing it almost €1 billion, while Germany is exploring whether to develop its own strategic stockpile. A separate Commission proposal to set up an EU-wide mechanism to carry out joint energy purchases was received without enthusiasm by EU leaders on Thursday, two diplomats said.
